issues.problem: Keeping the old cluster is described as a rollback capability without the operational prerequisites. After completed switchover old blue is forced read-only until the deployment resource is deleted, replication has stopped, and post-cutover writes are absent there. Automatic rollback of an unfinished switchover is a different operation.
issues.suggested_fix: Qualify old blue as a retained recovery starting point. Add an adjacent explanation of read-only release, connection rerouting and the disposition of post-cutover writes. Keep the limitation consistent with article 45 section 5.

issues.problem: Prose says three failures, the protected table says partial first run / failed second run / successful third run, and the next paragraph says two failures.

evidence.local: The fixed ADR 0025 at ae98df0953c0 also describes repeated failures but does not provide the individual CI logs; it does not resolve the internal inconsistency.

issues.suggested_fix: Keep the protected table and replace unsupported failure counts in prose with partial application and failures during preparation, unless per-run logs establish the count.

issues.problem: Cached connections are said to cause different writes in both clusters. Default post-switchover old blue cannot accept writes while the blue/green deployment resource exists.
issues.suggested_fix: Describe stale-connection read-only errors and reconnection failure as the default risk. Divergent writes require additional actions making old blue writable; do not present those actions as observed.

issues.problem: About six minutes does not match the displayed app-stop 17:20 to health-UP 17:24:40 interval, which is four minutes forty seconds.

issues.problem: Zero data loss exceeds the shown evidence: pre-cutover row counts of six tables and post-cutover successful requests do not establish every historical row value or every missing write.

evidence.local: Article 47 itself explains why later comparisons cannot prove every pre-cutover write.

issues.suggested_fix: Use no sign of loss within the checked scope, followed by the actual checks. Keep a universal zero-loss statement only with additional evidence.

issues.location: Protected alarm table line 291 and explanation line 295; related article 51 lines 241-243

Aurora T4g is configured for Unlimited: exhausted earned credits do not by themselves imply Standard-mode automatic CPU throttling. Article 51 leaves the applicable mode vague. The same protected block gives 0-to-100 credits as about three hours without its idle-CPU assumption; observed +6 credits/hour elsewhere would take about 16.7 hours, not three.

Keep gross earned credits distinct from net balance change.

issues.location: Patch-version paragraph line 187 and summary line 258
issues.problem: The 8.0.43-or-later to 8.0.42 example is presented as a downgrade that cannot reuse the datadir. Official MySQL 8.0 documentation supports in-place downgrades within 8.0 starting with 8.0.35. This differs from unsupported 8.0 to 5.7 downgrade.
issues.suggested_fix: Remove the general unsupported-datadir inference. Keep the actual issue: an unpinned tag can make the restoration/test version differ from the intended version. Whether 8.0.43 was actually downloaded remains unverified. Cite a specific restriction if one existed.

issues.location: Protected docker run and readiness loop; lines 74-84
issues.problem: The fresh official mysql container command supplies neither initialization credentials nor an existing initialized datadir. As shown it does not satisfy initialization requirements, and the following unbounded readiness loop can wait indefinitely.
issues.suggested_fix: Add an adjacent note that authentication/volume configuration was omitted and this is not a standalone runnable command. Identify the loop as the SQL-readiness fragment, not a complete startup failure handler. Do not invent historical configuration.

issues.problem: KST 09:00 and UTC 00:00 represent the same instant. As timezone-free literal values created_at is nine hours smaller, yet the text says created_at is later and publication precedes creation.
issues.suggested_fix: Keep the example numbers but explain that differently expressed wall-clock values can appear nine hours apart without timezone context. Do not assert the opposite ordering. DATETIME is not automatically UTC-converted; CURRENT_TIMESTAMP follows the session timezone.

issues.problem: Calling SUM(CRC32(col)) deterministic across versions without conditions suggests content equivalence proof. Identical input representation is required, NULL handling and selected columns matter, and 32-bit collisions or sum cancellation remain possible.
issues.suggested_fix: Add the same limitation already used in article 49: this is a supplementary difference check over explicitly selected, consistently serialized values, not proof of complete equality.

issues.problem: Absence of --source-data does not alone make PITR impossible. Consistent backup coordinates can be captured another way, and --master-data is the older equivalent name; --source-data was introduced in 8.0.26.
issues.suggested_fix: Correct this immediately after the protected list: recovery needs a consistent backup baseline plus matching binlog position or GTID and available logs. Whether those were retained for this historical backup is unverified.

issues.problem: (page_id,version,id) does not completely replace (page_id,id) for every workload. The intervening version changes useful key order for page_id plus id ranges/order. Zero read benefit is unsupported.
issues.suggested_fix: Describe removal as the historical judgment and explicitly leave workload/EXPLAIN verification open. Do not claim complete redundancy without checking page_id-plus-id queries.

issues.problem: A 92-day request is said to automatically split into hourly, five-minute and one-minute segments. Retention resolution and requested Period are distinct. GetMetricStatistics aggregates by the requested Period; a start older than 63 days requires a multiple of 3600 seconds.
issues.suggested_fix: Label the protected diagram as available retention resolutions, not automatic mixed-period response behavior. State the actual query tool/Period/Statistics if available. 92*24 alone does not prove actual point count or Average aggregation.

issues.problem: The 1% duration conversion is followed by a claim that daily batch correlation was confirmed. Percentile boundaries and maxima cannot establish occurrence dates, continuous duration or causative jobs. Raw time series and job logs were not supplied.
issues.suggested_fix: Match article 52: 22 hours and about 15 minutes/day are scale conversions, not observed daily duration. Qualify the batch link as the contemporary interpretation/hypothesis unless the underlying time-series/log comparison is available.

issues.problem: Baseline 20% minus reader absorption 2-4 percentage points is not post-removal utilization, and the subtraction gives 16-18%, not the displayed 17-18%. The surrounding current average is 16.4%.
issues.suggested_fix: Mark the preserved formula as erroneous. A simple scenario adding the assumed reader increment to 16.4% gives 18.4-20.4%; identify this as an estimate awaiting measurement, not an executed result.

issues.problem: Ten microseconds is called physically impossible. The evidenced correction here is the CloudWatch metric unit, not a universal physical latency limit.
issues.suggested_fix: Add an adjacent explicit correction that the impossibility wording was unsupported. The documented fact is that WriteLatency is in seconds, so the recorded 0.01 converts to 10ms.

issues.problem: The 15-day one-minute retention limit is used as the reason for a minimum 15-day observation period. Retention is an available lookback limit, not a minimum experimental duration.
issues.suggested_fix: Separate workload-cycle-based observation duration from retention. If minute values must cover the full observation window, collect them before they age out.

limits: This is independent facts editing review in the code-reviewer role with official-document research; it does not replace the separate verifier source audit. Read BRIEF, PLAN, REVIEW, both designated skills and their referenced source/easy-read/SVG/template guidance; baseline, writers 043-053, checks, titles, technical-corrections and cost-redactions; and all current 43-53 article text, protected excerpts and SVG labels. Articles 52 and 53 were read after their writer completion records existed.

No live operations or historical experiments were rerun. No live AWS, DB, app, company Notion or Slack was accessed. Primary official documentation was retrieved with the web tool; present-day vendor behavior/calendar is as retrieved on 2026-10-24.

Source comparison prioritized fixed commits f13e8c2362cfaac706652eb532ced2d442486102, 82c7a847ed7a89c3900b2f2866463c2f77bb846a, f1bc455c4df9afbafdbccbf9eefa57b235de3bce and ae98df0953c0, including fixed ADR 0025 and ADR 0026. The read-only source repository had zero tracked changes at the initial check and four at the final check due to concurrent work; this reviewer performed no source writes. Private source filenames and paths are deliberately not copied.

Raw execution logs do not independently establish every outage boundary, successful request, row content, account-migration step, error-counter reset history, actual patch downgrade, actual rollback or reconnection sequence. The app-schema dump does not by itself migrate mysql.user; the reported account-preservation observation should not be expanded into that claim.

The original CloudWatch requests (tool, Period, Statistics, range splitting and missing-point treatment), raw metric points, CPU cumulative-use durations, batch logs, actual pool configuration and driver-specific SQL routing evidence were not supplied. Therefore actual tail duration, every-day occurrence, job causality, all-queries-to-writer routing and post-reader-removal results remain unverified. 92*24 is a theoretical time conversion, not evidence that 2208 points were actually returned.

Cost arithmetic used original values only transiently for comparison. This report retains ratios and factors, never original monetary amounts/unit rates, company identifiers or private source paths. Exact code-hash transitions are allowed only for the recorded cost exceptions; no additional code exception was assumed.

Protected-code errors are proposed for explicit nearby prose corrections; SVG text corrections should remain minimal. The leader owns integration and any expansion of protected-field exceptions. No article or shared setting was edited and no work was delegated.
